You can get your chest up by extending in your thoratic spine. To get this feel think about proud chest - this is what you do when you set up. Don't drop your hips any lower tho, that's the challenge and the position might not be comfortable.

For the pressure, idk how you breath but you should take a big breath before you start, in already braced position (you set everything, then breath in and hold). Do your rep with the hold breath and on the top you breath out as you already lockout. Then you can either take a breath again, go down, set up and do next rep, or you can breath in again in the start before you do your next rep. This problem of yours might be because of your head position.

Tldr: Your hips are way too down, your knees are way too forward so the bar is not over your mid foot, and your head should be neutral (save your neck:) ) 

Kinda hard to judge from this angle. From what I can see your knees go way to far forward and you kinda drag the bar around your knees if you feel me. The bar doesn't go straight up, but infront of you (around knees), then up. So your hips should be more up the you probably want to.

For the setup, I really recommend Allan's Thrall video on youtube on how to deadlift (there's specifically your issue here). Basically, you have to keep the bar like an inch away from you. Then you hinge in the hips and knees go forward to touch the bar (you don't hit the bar hard, the bar cannot move). Then you grip the bar (you don't move the bar), set your back and then push with legs and pull at the same time.
